History of Present Illness:
___ yo male with history of diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and 
ESRD on HD was admitted from the ED with recurrent hypoglycemia. 
This admission he was found down at home with a fingerstick of 
28 after proper insulin administration per ___ 
recommendations. 
.
Of note, the patient was just discharged 2 days prior for the 
same complaint of syncope secondary to hypoglycemia. On the last 
admission, he was found down at home with a fingerstick of 38. 
At that time, he checked his fingerstick before breakfast and it 
was 141, took insulin, ate breakfast, and next thing he knew he 
was on the floor. His fingersticks were monitored during that 
admission with insulin ___ 15 units at breakfast and 10 units 
at dinner. His fingerstick ranged from in the 150-200s on that 
regimen. At that time, patient was recommended by social work to 
be placed given his multiple admissions for poor blood glucose 
control; however the patient refused and was discharged to home 
with ___ services. Prior to discharge, his diabetes teaching was 
explained to him in ___ and with ___ language teaching 
materials.   
.
On the day prior to this admission, the patient was staying at 
his sister's house and being watched carefully. Since his 
discharge 2 days prior, she has been taking his fingersticks and 
administering his insulin which are predrawn by ___. The dosing 
of insulin that was being administered is correct per the last 
___ visit/discharge summary. Per the sister, on 
___ which was a HD day, AM fingerstick was 152 -> the 
patient received 10U humulog ___ -> had breakfast of juice, 
cornflakes, and yogurt -> then pre dinner ___ of 182 -> 5U -> ate 
a little for dinner. No episodes or symptoms of hypoglycemia on 
___. Then, today on ___ which was the morning of admission, 
the patient's AM fingerstick was 183 at 8:30am, prebreakfast BS 
was 153 -> 15U ___ -> the patient ate cornflakes, yogurt for 
breakfast, and then did not feel hungry and only snacked on 
cornflakes and juice instead of lunch. The patient was able to 
remember the morning's events up until lying in bed in mid 
morning.The patient remembers having some diaphoresis, dizziness 
which is similar to prior episodes of hypoglycemia, but did not 
have sweets on him and then blacked out. He was found down by 
his family with a BS of 28 at home.
.
In the field, the patient's HR was 120, SBP was 130, RR 12, 97% 
on RA. The patient was given 1mg of glucagon, then was AxO 
without complaints. Initial BS in the ED was 103 at 13:45, then 
204 at 15:20. The patient was admitted for further workup for 
recurrent hypoglycemia. 
. 
On arrival to the floor, the patient was doing well with no 
complaints. He denies diaphoresis, palpitations, shakiness, 
chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, chills, cough, or 
dysuria. He is mentating well and notes that the episode this 
morning was scary for him.

8am     ___ yo male with Diabetes Mellitus, ESRD on HD, and chronic 
systolic heart failure was admitted with recurrent 
hypoglycemia/syncope 2 days s/p recent hospitalization for 
hypoglycemia. His hospital course is presented below by problem.

1. Hypoglycemia/Poor control of DMI - With his multiple hospital 
visits in the past several months for uncontrolled DMI, the 
patient has proved to have difficulty controlling his blood 
sugars and managing his insulin regimen at home. Since his last 
discharge from a hospitalization for the same chief complaint of 
syncope and hypoglycemia, he has been living with his sister and 
monitored closely. The sister brought in the pre-mixed insulin 
syringes drawn up by ___ and the dosing administered was correct 
per the last ___ recommendations of 15 units QAM/10units QPM 
of NPH ___ and decreased to 10 units QAM/5 units QPM on HD 
days. The patient was seen both by the ___ diabetes service 
and by the Renal team during this hospital stay and the 
consensus was that the goal for this patient is not tight 
diabetes control but to come up with a manageable regimen to 
avoid hypoglycemia in this patient with decreased insight on how 
to manage his blood. The reasons are that the patient is already 
on HD for ESRD and has complications from blindness and 
difficulty administering/adjusting medications at home. His 
insulin was switched from NPH ___ to longer acting lantus. He 
was started on 5U lantus and 1 unit humalog TID with meals. The 
plan was to give 1U humalog with all meals to simplify his 
regimen. As the patient's blood sugars ran slightly high between 
198-397 on the 5 units of lantus, his lantus was titrated up to 
6 units QAM daily. The patient was discharged with same-day 
follow up at the ___. He was also set up with 
additional diabetes nutrition education with ___ interpreter 
at ___ on ___.
  
2. ESRD on HD. The patient was continued HD per home schedule. 
He was also followed by the renal service while in the hospital. 
His phosphorus and PTH were both high. His lanthanum was 
increased from 1000mg TID with meals to 1,500mg TID with meals. 
His multivitamin was also discontinued. He will need follow up 
on his increased PTH by his PCP or renal physician.
 
3. Hypertension. His blood pressures were stable and slightly 
elevated on this admission. He was continued on his regimen of 
nitrate, diuretics, and afterload reducer. However, this 
complicated regimen can also be titrated/simplified by his PCP 
as an outpatient if indicated.  

4. Chronic Systolic Heart Failure EF 40-45%. While in the 
hospital, the patient was euvolemic and continued on his ___, 
beta blocker, and diuretic  

5. GERD - Stable. He was continued on his PPI

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted when you were found unconscious at home with 
low blood sugars. You were brought to the hospital where we 
adjusted your insulin medications to prevent these episodes of 
low blood sugars. 

These are your new medication changes:
- You are now on new types of insulin. Your new regimen is 
long-acting lantus 6 units with breakfast, with 1 unit of fast 
acting humalog insulin before each meal.
- We stopped your multivitamin
- We increased your lanthanum dose with each meal
- Please take the rest of your medications as directed

*** It is very important that you keep candy/sugar with you at 
all times and take this if you feel shaky, sweaty, faint, 
lightheaded, or have any of your normal symptoms of low sugar 
levels.

Please try to take measurements of your blood sugar at home and 
bring this into your ___ and primary care appointments. If 
you have any levels that are too low or too high, please call 
them immediately for directions.
